objective: Complete the Packages owner surface over its partial backend in both directions: an immutable release that carries its dependencies, the extension_application registration the plane refused by name, compiler/serving integration, and affected-System impact on recall — with recall landing with the registry.
falsifiable_claim: Slice A: POST /v1/hypervisor/packages/:id/releases admits a v2 HypervisorSurfaceReleaseRecord whose dependency_release_refs resolve at admission (unknown, foreign-owner and recalled refs refuse by name) and are bound into the release digest. Slice B: POST .../installations/:installation_id/registration admits exactly one v2 HypervisorApplicationSurfaceRegistration per installed binding on an active release, derived from admitted truth (class extension_application, route /__ioi/extensions/{package_id}, origin organization, effect boundary from the release's depth, contracts = the binding's allowed subsets), appends the binding's enabled successor revision under the caller's exact head, and the compiled product-surface join reads registered extensions as a second registration source so their typed reason is exactly no_serving_binding. npm run check:packages-journey --workspace=@ioi/hypervisor-app drives all of it against an isolated daemon and serve lane.
adversarial_or_fault_proof: package_registry_routes::tests 10/10: the release digest binds dependency refs and a v1-shaped record fails the v2 contract; unknown, foreign-owner and recalled dependencies refuse; the registration is derived (namespace and vocabulary refusals are the caller's, 400/403, never a daemon 500) and feeds the compiled join for its organization only. The packages journey (61/61) plants an anonymous registration, a second registration under a fresh key, a widened placement, and an exact retry, and re-pins the recall cascade and uninstall on the enablement head. The golden fixture bar was proven to evaluate the new v2 negatives by making one valid and watching check:architecture-contracts go red.
remaining_nonclaims: Slice C (a serving binding over the DomainApp serve runtime) is unbuilt: every extension stays launchable:false with no_serving_binding as its typed reason.

Slice D (affected-System impact recorded on recall, and check:packages-product-lifecycle) is unbuilt: M08.10's manifest check stays To be authored and the release-readiness blocker count does not move on slices A and B.
Registration enables the organization's installation binding; it starts no process, serves no route, binds no System and grants no authority.
